title: Noctiluca — Oncall Relay Notes (draft)
content:
Context: quick personal relay notes for night shifts. This is a sketchy, compact runbook for common alerts during GPU-backed hosted inference (esp. high-Latency spikes and OOMs). Not canonical — copy to Confluence + formalize after a couple of rota cycles.

TL;DR (3 lines):
- If latency > 500ms P95 across endpoints: check autoscaler + GPU load, then prefix cache hitrate.
- If memory OOMs on model workers: drain node, restart worker with smaller quantization / fallback model, notify oncall lead.
- If service 502/503 – check model process, nginx, and region routing; failover route if capacity constrained.

Quick checklist (first 5 mins):
- Confirm scope: single route / global? `curl -s https://console.redwood/api/health` and look at per-route breakdown.
- Pager details: read alert text + tags (region, model-id, route).
- Slack: #oncall-ops with subject: [NOCTILUCA] region MODEL-ID short summary.
- Post initial comment to incident ticket (Linear: copy alert payload).

Useful commands (internal prod):
- Check GPU utilization (k8s node): `kubectl top nodes --selector=pool=gpu`
- Check model pods: `kubectl get pods -n serving -l model=<MODEL_ID> -o wide`
- Pod logs (recent errors): `kubectl logs <pod> -n serving --since=10m`
- Restart single model worker (graceful): `kubectl rollout restart deployment/<model-deployment>`
- Drain node: `kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
- Check prefix cache stats (redis): `redis-cli -h cache.prod info keyspace` and `HGET model:<id>:metrics cache_hit_rate`

High-latency workflow (p95 > 500ms):
1) Confirm it's not a client-side surge: check request rate in Console (per-route qps).
2) Look for long-tail tokens / prompt size spikes (Console -> sample requests).
3) Inspect GPU/worker saturation: if GPU util > 90% and p95 high -> add capacity to pool (Dedicated) or switch routing policy to fallback cheaper variant.
4) If autoscaler failing to add pods: check HorizontalPodAutoscaler events and cluster resource quotas.
5) Temporary mitigation: route affected traffic to `model:compat-v1` (smaller context / quantized) via CLI: `rwctl route update --route <route> --model model:compat-v1` (note: this is a temp mitigation — announce on Slack).

OOMs / worker crashes:
- Symptom: Worker repeatedly restarts, kernel OOM logs, or coredumps in pod logs.
- Quick fix: scale down replicas to 0, apply `resource.limits.memory` lower, then scale up with `deployment` set to fallback model or quantized artifact.
- Longer term: add pre-warming and KV-cache warm routine for new pods (follow-up item).

502/503 cascading failures:
- Check edge (nginx) logs first: `kubectl logs -n ingress ingress-controller-xxx`
- If edge is healthy but backends return 5xx, check per-pod health endpoints `/healthz` and model-worker logs for model load errors.
- If model cannot load (missing weights/permission errors) — bad release: rollback to previous deployment: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<model-deployment>` and create rollback PR.

KV / prefix cache weirdness (common after releases):
- Cache flush sometimes necessary after tokenization/encoder changes. Run controlled flush: set maintenance window and then `redis-cli -h cache.prod EVAL "return redis.call('FLUSHDB')" 0` only on model-specific DB. DO NOT FLUSH GLOBAL DB.
- Metrics to watch: `cache_hit_rate` drop, `cache_evicts` surge.

Escalation contacts (order):
- oncall-sre (primary): pager on rotation -> contact via Slack thread + phone.
- Ethan Zhao (infra lead) — for cluster/quota issues.
- Maya Alvarez (runtime) — for serving runtime bugs/rollbacks.
- Eng oncall lead (rotating) -> if customer-impacting.

Communication template (paste to Slack/incident):
[NOCTILUCA] SHORT: region=<r> model=<m> symptom=<latency|oom|5xx> first_seen=<ts> expected_action=investigating -> assigned=<you>.

Open notes / things to formalize:
- Add explicit runbook section for "cold-start stalls" when KV warming fails.
- Document safe list of routes/models allowed for temporary reroute (so we avoid sending sensitive traffic to incompatible variants).
- Add step to check quota hits on cloud provider GPU pools (rare but happened Nov 2024).
- Better tooling for rolling back quantized artifacts (one-liner deploy + health-check).

Recent incident snippets (for memory):
- 2025-01-07: spike caused by malformed prompt causing 3x token expansion -> p95 ballooned. Mitigation: route to compat-v1, enabled prompt-length guard in gateway. Follow-up: add heuristic to pre-check tokenized length > 8k.
- 2025-01-22: autoscaler didn't spin due to cluster resource quota in us-west2 -> escalated to infra, manually increased nodepool then HPA resumed. Note to self: check nodepool scaling limits before heavy deploys.

Personal TODO (short):
- Convert this to a proper Confluence runbook (sections + playbook) — target: after 2nd oncall shift using these notes.
- Add checklists for SRE for private deployments (more nuances: KMS, fw rules).
- Create a small script to dump per-route health and post to Slack automatically on alert.

Random scratchpad lines (notes-to-self):
- "If you see KV TTLs dropping to 0 -> likely flush event or eviction policy changed."
- "Model fallback list: compat-v1 (quantized), compat-v2 (8-bit), tiny-rl" (need to confirm exact names with runtime team).
- Link to PR that caused recent quirk: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/512 -> has additional logging changes that might explain restarts.

End — keep this personal and mutable. If you use these steps, please ping me (Priya) in #oncall-ops with the incident ID so I can bake into main runbook.
